title: BrightLedger x Redwood - Monthly check-in (usage insights + exports)
summary: BrightLedger reviewed month-over-month spend increases and asked for (1) chargeback by route/service, (2) weekly automated exports (CSV/JSON), and (3) clarity on data freshness vs billing accuracy and how long route-level data is retained. Redwood aligned on upcoming in-console Usage Insights (cost drivers by route/model), export limits/guardrails, and guidance for route tagging + naming to avoid cardinality blowups. Open questions were around invoice reconciliation, cached-token fields, and whether exports can be scheduled vs manually triggered in v1.
questions: Can we get a weekly export automatically (scheduled), not manual download?
How fresh is route-level cost data (near real time vs daily close)?
How long do you retain route/model aggregates and exportable data?
Will the export include cached token counts and unit cost fields?
If smart routing falls back to another model, is cost still attributed to the same route?
Why doesn’t console cost match our invoice totals day-by-day?
action_items: Dev Patel (Redwood) - Send BrightLedger the route tagging guidance draft + naming conventions (avoid user IDs in route). Due: 2026-02-20
Paula Mendes (Redwood) - Confirm initial GA export limitations (max time range / rows) and whether scheduled exports are on the near-term roadmap. Due: 2026-02-24
Nadia Rahman (Redwood) - Provide a short explanation of freshness vs accuracy and how late metering is handled (shareable blurb for FinOps). Due: 2026-02-24
Jon Patel (BrightLedger) - Add route identifiers to their 3 main services ("ledger-ingest", "support-chat", "invoice-qa") and report back on Unknown route %. Due: 2026-02-28
Maya Hernandez (BrightLedger) - Share a sample of their current internal chargeback CSV format (columns + grouping) so Redwood can align export schema. Due: 2026-02-28
next_steps: Redwood to follow up with documentation and a short write-up on reconciliation expectations (console vs invoice).
BrightLedger to enable consistent route tagging across their workloads and reduce "Unknown route" volume.
Schedule a 30-min follow-up in ~2 weeks to review early usage insights screens and validate export format requirements.
transcript_text:
Fireflies.ai Meeting Transcript

Title: BrightLedger x Redwood - Monthly check-in (usage insights + exports)
Recorded: 2026-02-19 16:00 PT
Duration: 43 min

Attendees
- Dev Patel (Redwood Inference)
- Paula Mendes (Redwood Inference)
- Nadia Rahman (Redwood Inference)
- Sarah Kim (BrightLedger, FinOps)
- Jon Patel (BrightLedger, Eng Manager)
- Maya Hernandez (BrightLedger, Data)

---

[00:00] Dev Patel: Cool, I think we’re all here. Sarah, Jon, Maya — good to see you again. Main agenda I had was usage trends from the last 30 days, and then we can spend time on the exports / chargeback topic. Does that work?

[00:13] Sarah Kim: Yep. That’s the big one for us. We’re getting pressure from finance to allocate spend by product line, and right now it’s like… we have totals but not where it’s coming from.

[00:25] Jon Patel: And honestly we’re trying to avoid building our own like… token meter pipeline. We can do it, but we’d rather not.

[00:33] Dev Patel: Totally. That’s aligned with what we’re building. Paula and Nadia joined because they’re closest to the “usage insights” work.

[00:41] Paula Mendes: Hey everyone.

[00:42] Nadia Rahman: Hi.

[00:45] Dev Patel: Quick recap of what we saw: your overall token volume is up about… 18-ish percent month over month. The big spike was around the invoice Q&A feature rollout, right?

[00:56] Jon Patel: Yeah, we moved it from internal-only to GA for customers.

[01:01] Maya Hernandez: The support chat also got more traffic.

[01:04] Dev Patel: Makes sense. Sarah, you mentioned on email the main thing is weekly reporting. Can you say what “good” looks like? Like, columns, grouping, cadence.

[01:15] Sarah Kim: So weekly, per environment would be nice — prod vs staging. And we want to split by service route. Like “/api/support/chat” versus “/api/invoice/qa”, something like that. Then within that, model. If we can get it. Because we run different model sizes.

[01:33] Sarah Kim: Today we do cost allocation manually: total spend divided by request counts, which is… not great.

[01:40] Paula Mendes: That’s basically the exact question the new console page is meant to answer: top cost drivers by route, and then which models drive that spend.

[01:47] Jon Patel: When you say route, do you mean URL path? Or like a tag we set?

[01:52] Nadia Rahman: Good question. It can be either. The recommended path is you set a route identifier in the SDK or via header, and if it’s not present we can derive from the gateway path. But derivation gets tricky with dynamic segments.

[02:06] Jon Patel: Yeah, we have things like /customer/12345/invoice. That would explode.

[02:10] Nadia Rahman: Exactly. We normalize / recommend templates like /customer/:id/invoice or better, a stable name like “invoice-qa”. We’re putting guardrails because cardinality can blow up the aggregates.

[02:26] Sarah Kim: For chargeback, we’d prefer stable names anyway. Product lines map to a few services. “invoice-qa” and “support-chat” is fine.

[02:35] Dev Patel: Ok. So for you, ideal is: weekly report, route dimension, model dimension, and cost fields.

[02:43] Maya Hernandez: And latency maybe? Not for finance, but for us.

[02:46] Dev Patel: Yep. That should be in-console at least: p50/p95 by route.

[02:52] Sarah Kim: We also need to answer “what changed.” Like, why did spend jump this week.

[03:00] Paula Mendes: The UI will have a week-over-week delta view, and in route detail you’ll see “top models” and change vs prior period.

[03:09] Jon Patel: Do you have an ETA?

[03:11] Paula Mendes: We’re targeting a beta soon. I can’t promise a date on this call, but it’s weeks not quarters.

[03:19] Dev Patel: Yeah, and I’ll loop you into the beta if you’re open to it.

[03:23] Sarah Kim: Yes. But I need to be clear: we need exports. Like an actual CSV we can hand to finance. Screenshots don’t help.

[03:32] Paula Mendes: Understood. Export is part of the scope — CSV and JSON.

[03:37] Sarah Kim: Is it “download when I click a button” or “I can schedule it every Monday at 8am”?

[03:44] Dev Patel: Today, the first version is likely manual export from the console. Scheduling is a separate feature; we’ve heard it a lot though.

[03:53] Jon Patel: Could we call an API for export generation? Like we have our own scheduler.

[03:59] Nadia Rahman: There will be an export job API internally; the question is what’s exposed at GA and what’s behind the UI. But conceptually yes: create export job with filters, then download.

[04:13] Sarah Kim: Ok, so we could still automate with a script, if it’s exposed.

[04:17] Paula Mendes: That’s a product decision we’re still finalizing. We also have to do RBAC and audit logging because exports can leak data across projects if it’s not scoped right.

[04:30] Sarah Kim: Audit logging matters for us too. We’ve had security ask “who exported what.”

[04:35] Dev Patel: Yep. We’re implementing audit events for export creation and download. Like user, time, filters. That’s in the plan.

[04:45] Maya Hernandez: Can I ask about retention? How far back will we be able to see route-level breakdown?

[04:51] Nadia Rahman: There’s two things: raw request telemetry retention, and aggregated rollups. Rollups can be kept longer. We’re still aligning on exact numbers for GA, but expect the route-level insights to be based on aggregates, not full raw logs.

[05:08] Sarah Kim: But if we need an export for, like, a quarterly close, we need at least 90 days.

[05:13] Paula Mendes: I hear you. We have to balance storage and compliance. But 90 days is a common ask. Let me take that back; I don’t want to state a policy incorrectly.

[05:25] Dev Patel: For now, from support side, what we can do is ensure you have a weekly export so you can store it on your side. Even if retention is shorter in the console.

[05:34] Sarah Kim: That works. As long as it’s consistent.

[05:37] Jon Patel: Another question: how fresh is the data? If we look at today’s spend at 2pm, will it be accurate?

[05:45] Nadia Rahman: It depends what you mean by accurate. The pipeline is near-real-time-ish, but token metering can be late arriving for some paths (streaming, retries). So we generally say: you’ll see data within minutes, but it can settle over a few hours. For billing-grade, invoices are computed on a different system with its own close.

[06:07] Sarah Kim: That’s the mismatch we’ve been seeing — console vs invoice.

[06:11] Dev Patel: Right. And we’ve been trying to set expectations: the console is operational + directional, invoice is authoritative. The new views will show “freshness” and maybe a note like “data can update.”

[06:24] Maya Hernandez: So week-over-week comparisons could shift?

[06:27] Nadia Rahman: Slightly, yes, if late events land. Usually it’s small.

[06:33] Jon Patel: What about cached tokens? We saw in some docs you count cached tokens separately.

[06:39] Paula Mendes: The plan is to break out input tokens, output tokens, cached tokens, and then cost fields. But the exact schema in exports — we’re trying to keep it stable so finance scripts don’t break.

[06:54] Sarah Kim: We need cached tokens because we’re trying to measure savings from prefix caching.

[06:59] Nadia Rahman: Yep. We track that in metering. The one caveat is depending on model and runtime, cached tokens might be estimated. But it’s useful.

[07:12] Dev Patel: Jon, on the route dimension: are you already setting anything like that in requests?

[07:18] Jon Patel: Not consistently. We have a header for internal tracing, but not in Redwood SDK. We use mostly Python for invoice Q&A, and TS for support chat.

[07:28] Nadia Rahman: Good, that’s workable. We’re adding route tagging support across SDKs. It will likely be a “route” parameter or a standard header. We’ll share the guidance.

[07:41] Jon Patel: We can do it. The bigger issue is making sure product teams don’t stick user IDs in it.

[07:47] Paula Mendes: Totally. We’ll include best practices and also hard limits: length, allowed chars, and we can roll up to “other” if cardinality exceeds budget.

[08:00] Sarah Kim: If it rolls up to “other”, does that break chargeback?

[08:04] Nadia Rahman: Only if routes are too many or dynamic. If you keep it to a controlled set — which it sounds like you will — it won’t roll up.

[08:14] Maya Hernandez: What about “Unknown route”? We saw that in some early screenshots you sent.

[08:19] Dev Patel: Unknown route basically means no tag. In your case, until you add tags, you’ll see Unknown dominating.

[08:27] Jon Patel: That’s consistent with what we see.

[08:30] Sarah Kim: Ok. So step one for us is to tag routes. Step two is exports.

[08:35] Dev Patel: Yep.

[08:37] Paula Mendes: Can I ask how you want to slice chargeback? By route only, or route + project? Because in Redwood you might have multiple projects.

[08:46] Sarah Kim: Ideally project and route. But if that’s hard, route within prod project is enough.

[08:54] Jon Patel: We have prod and staging as separate projects. Region doesn’t matter for finance.

[09:00] Nadia Rahman: Cool, that matches the filter model: time range, project, env, region, deployment mode.

[09:08] Dev Patel: Another point we’ve seen: sometimes smart routing can switch models mid-request. You asked for model breakdown; do you need “requested model” or “served model”?

[09:20] Jon Patel: Served model. If it fell back to something else, that’s the actual cost.

[09:25] Nadia Rahman: Yep. The event schema includes served model, and we still attribute it back to the same route.

[09:33] Sarah Kim: Wait—so if it retries and goes to a different region, it still stays the same route bucket?

[09:38] Nadia Rahman: Yes. Route is from request context. Retries still count toward that same route.

[09:45] Maya Hernandez: That’s good.

[09:48] Dev Patel: On weekly exports: Sarah, do you have a standard format finance expects?

[09:54] Sarah Kim: We usually do: week_start, week_end, cost_usd, service_name, environment, and then optional columns like model, tokens_in, tokens_out.

[10:07] Paula Mendes: Ok. And you want a line per (route, model) for that window?

[10:12] Sarah Kim: Yes. Or route totals plus a separate tab for models, but that’s optional.

[10:19] Dev Patel: For v1, it’ll probably be one dataset with both dims, plus you can filter.

[10:24] Jon Patel: Any limits on export size?

[10:27] Paula Mendes: There will be limits. We’re still setting the exact guardrails, but think “bounded.” Like time range max and row count max, to avoid timeouts.

[10:38] Sarah Kim: That’s fine as long as weekly works.

[10:41] Maya Hernandez: We tried exporting other reports and it times out when it’s big.

[10:46] Dev Patel: Yeah, that’s a common issue. Exports will be async job based, so you request, it generates, then you download.

[10:55] Jon Patel: Perfect.

[10:58] Sarah Kim: One more question: we need this for internal incident reviews too. Like “spend doubled because of X deploy.” Will you show deltas?

[11:07] Paula Mendes: The route detail view will show “what changed” for the time window compared to prior. It’s not full anomaly detection, but it’s a start.

[11:17] Dev Patel: And if you have a specific incident, we can help pull the export and attach it to the review.

[11:23] Sarah Kim: Great.

[11:25] (crosstalk)

[11:26] Maya Hernandez: Sorry, can I ask about token pricing vs GPU time? Like is there a GPU metric too?

[11:33] Nadia Rahman: We have a GPU time proxy for some deployments, but for Hosted API we mostly do token-based. The insights will show token counts and total cost, and if GPU time proxy is available we can display it.

[11:48] Jon Patel: We’re hosted, so tokens are fine.

[11:51] Dev Patel: Ok.

[12:00] Dev Patel: Let’s do a quick recap and next steps. First, Jon will add route tags to your top 3 routes: invoice-qa, support-chat, ledger-ingest. Second, I’ll send you the SDK guidance doc we have so far.

[12:15] Jon Patel: Yep.

[12:16] Dev Patel: Paula will take back the retention and export automation question, like whether we can expose the export job API or do scheduled exports.

[12:26] Paula Mendes: Yep. I’ll also confirm what the initial limits will be.

[12:30] Dev Patel: Nadia will send a short explanation for finance: freshness vs accuracy, and why invoice might not match console day to day.

[12:38] Nadia Rahman: Yeah, I can write that up.

[12:41] Sarah Kim: That would be helpful. Finance hates “because reasons.”

[12:45] Dev Patel: (laughs) Totally.

[12:48] Maya Hernandez: I’ll share our current chargeback CSV format. It’s pretty simple.

[12:53] Dev Patel: Perfect.

[12:55] Dev Patel: Any other questions before we drop?

[12:58] Jon Patel: Just confirm — route tagging won’t break anything? Like it’s optional.

[13:03] Nadia Rahman: Optional. If you don’t set it, you’ll just see Unknown route.

[13:07] Jon Patel: Great.

[13:09] Sarah Kim: Ok. Thanks everyone.

[13:11] Dev Patel: Thanks.

---

Auto-generated Notes (Fireflies)
- Main ask: weekly exports for chargeback by route + model.
- Concerns: retention window, data freshness vs invoice accuracy, and whether exports can be scheduled/automated.
- Recommendation: add stable route identifiers via SDK/header; avoid dynamic path values to prevent cardinality issues.
